[iOS][CPE] Dismiss and deallocate passkeyNavigationController on exit

Unlike listCoordinator and consentCoordinator,
passkeyNavigationController was never dismissed, cleared, or set to nil
when CredentialProviderViewController completed a request, exited with
an error code, or entered the background. This caused
passkeyNavigationController and any pushed view controllers (such as
reauthentication web views) to remain strongly retained in memory after
the Credential Provider Extension was dismissed.

- Add -cleanUpPresentedUI to stop consentCoordinator and
  listCoordinator and dismiss, clear, and nil out
  _passkeyNavigationController.
- Call -cleanUpPresentedUI on all extension completion and exit paths.
- Set presentationController.delegate = self on
  passkeyNavigationController.
- Observe UIApplicationDidEnterBackgroundNotification and
  NSExtensionHostDidEnterBackgroundNotification to cancel the extension
  request and tear down presented UI when backgrounded.

CONV=87dc3524-a99e-4e3b-8165-11c5d1b95873

[Android] Trim unused locale .pak and aapt resources in test APKs

Previously, instrumentation test APKs built via
chrome_common_apk_or_module_tmpl packaged all 83 platform locales in
both assets/locales/*.pak (52.6 MB uncompressed) and resources.arsc
(34.7 MB), even though integration tests only exercise a small set of
locales.

Restrict instrumentation test APKs to 16 representative locales plus
pseudolocales via chrome_test_apk_locales and chrome_test_apk_pak_assets
(reusing outputs from :chrome_apk_paks), and share
chrome_test_apk_pak_assets with android_browsertests in place of
android_browsertests_locale_pak_assets.

Measured impact: Shrinks ChromePublicTest.apk from 549 MB to 480 MB (-69
MB / -12.6%), saving ~3.9 GB of aggregate CAS/ADB payload across 56
Swarming shards per CQ build.

Test: IncognitoNewTabPageTest*, LanguageSettingsTest*,

[3p freshness] wayland-protocols: Move plasma-wayland-protocols to kde/src

Move the plasma-wayland-protocols submodule from wayland-protocols/kde
to wayland-protocols/kde/src, and give it its own
wayland-protocols/kde/README.chromium, so that it follows the standard
directory structure that the Skia Autoroller expects (README.chromium
next to a src/ submodule). BUILD.gn now reads the protocols from
kde/src/src/protocols/.

No version change: the submodule stays at 0b07950714b3 (v1.3.0).

Existing checkouts: upstream has its own src/ directory, so kde/src/
already exists there as a plain directory. `gclient sync` moves it to
_bad_scm/ and checks out the submodule; the rest of the old checkout
stays untracked in kde/. To clean up, run
`rm -rf third_party/wayland-protocols/kde && gclient sync`.

[bfcache] Reland WPT test for WebLocks grant to a worker in BFCache

https://crrev.com/c/7894097 added a WPT test verifying that a WebLock
granted to a dedicated worker in BFCache has its callback deferred
until the page is restored from BFCache, and was later reverted in
https://crrev.com/c/8274931 due to an Android WebView regression.

Now that https://crrev.com/c/8526329 routes TaskType::kWebLocks to the
pausable task queue on frames and workers, reland the WPT test to
provide end-to-end BFCache coverage for dedicated workers.

[Webium] Decide the Glic and avatar button visibility per frame

The WebUIDataSource of the WebUI toolbar is shared by all toolbars in
the same BrowserContext. With kTopChromeWebUISharedRenderer, the
toolbars of the windows of all profiles will be created in
TopChromeWebUIProfile, so the data source must not have values that
depend on the profile of the window: they would come from whichever
toolbar was created last.

Whether the Glic and avatar buttons can be shown depends on the
profile. Keep only the feature flags in the data source, and set the
profile checks, GlicEnabling::IsProfileEligible() and
AvatarToolbarButtonInterface::CanShowForProfile(), in the initial
state of each frame, which WebUIToolbarUI::WebUIRenderFrameCreated()
computes from the user profile of the WebContents.

No behavior change: the same checks run for the same profile, and are
only delivered per frame instead of through the shared data source.

arc: input_overlay: Keep DataController storage in profile dir

DataController::GetFilePathFromPackageName() appended the ARC package
name directly onto the per-profile google_gio storage directory. Require
the package name to be a single non-empty path component (not absolute,
no parent references, equal to its own BaseName) and return an empty
FilePath otherwise. ReadProtoFromFile() and WriteProtoToFile() now
early-return on an empty path so file operations stay within the storage
directory.

Add DataControllerTest covering valid and rejected package names and
verifying that file operations stay within the storage directory.

[contextual-tasks] Split App_Composebox_BasicMode into nested suites

ContextualTasksBrowserTest.App_Composebox_BasicMode runs 12 active
Mocha test cases sequentially in a single IN_PROC_BROWSER_TEST_F, where
each test mounts <contextual-tasks-app> and initializes a <webview>
guest. On slower and debug builders (such as Linux Tests (dbg)(1)),
each Mocha test takes 6-9 seconds, causing the combined suite to exceed
the browser_tests timeout (~95-100s).

Split ContextualTasksAppComposeboxBasicModeTest into four nested suites
(ZOrderAndHistory, NavigationFromAiPage, PendingBasicMode, and
NlmAndOnboardingTooltip) and run each nested suite in its own
IN_PROC_BROWSER_TEST_F so each group has its own per-test time budget.
Also await Lit update completion after Mojo flushes and isolate thread
frame navigation events in the remaining navigation tests.

[a11y-android] Reland: Remove ignored check in IsNodeValid

This is a reland of reverted CL: crrev.com/c/8651881
The first patch set is the reverted CL and the next has the fix.

crrev.com/c/8256250 added `!node->IsIgnored()` to `IsNodeValid` to
prevent crashes when operating on ignored nodes. However, using this
check in `WebContentsAccessibilityImpl.handleFocusChanged` causes
accessibility focus to reset to root during dynamic DOM and SPA
transitions when nodes are temporarily ignored.

crrev.com/c/8573418 subsequently added explicit ignored-node guards to
`PopulateAccessibilityNodeInfo`, `UpdateCachedAccessibilityNodeInfo`,
and `GetSelectionAsTextOffsetsForNode`, while `SetExtendedSelection`
remains guarded. `IsNodeValid` can therefore safely return to an
existence check (`GetAXFromUniqueID(id) != nullptr`).

A regression test is added to ensure operations on ignored nodes remain
properly guarded.

Remove kNativeViewHostManagesLayers and associated dead code

This has been enabled from 3 month, so let's remove the
legacy code path in next branch m158 (next monday).

Remove views::features::kNativeViewHostManagesLayers and enable the
managed layer path unconditionally everywhere. Also remove obsolete
flags, legacy window reordering logic, dead layer tracking from
Widget and View, and unused top insets hit-testing logic from
NativeViewHost and ImmersiveModeControllerChromeos.

NativeViewHost::SetLayerManagedByViews(false) is retained for
arc::CustomTab on ChromeOS, and SetCreateLayer(false) is retained
for ArcNotificationContentView on ChromeOS.

Avoid dangling ActionAppMenuMetrics pointer in AppMenuZoomView

Entering fullscreen from AppMenuZoomView closes and destroys
ActionAppMenu synchronously while MenuController::OnMouseReleased()
defers MenuRunnerImpl and AppMenuZoomView destruction on the stack,
leaving AppMenuZoomView::metrics_ dangling.

Replace AppMenuZoomView::metrics_ with an ExecuteCommandCallback bound
to ActionAppMenu's WeakPtr, matching AppMenuBlockView, and parameterize
AppMenuFullscreenButtonInteractiveTest over kAppMenuGlowUp.

The flag has expired and been removed from chrome://flags.
This CL removes the flag entry from flag-metadata.json, about_flags.cc,
flag_descriptions.h, and features.{h,cc}.

It also cleans up the associated dead code:

  IsPlatformEligibleForSyncCheckerCheckAllowlist()

  AsyncCheckTracker and its callers across tab features and browser
  clients.

  BrowserURLLoaderThrottle for sync check.
- Removes obsolete tests and test coverage for the flag.

[Reading mode PDFs] Treat thin filled rectangles as ruling lines

Pass the filled rectangles from `PDFiumPage::GetFilledRectInfo()` to
`PdfAccessibilityTreeBuilder` through
`AccessibilityPageObjects::filled_rects`. In
`PdfAccessibilityTree::IsDataFromPluginValid()`, reject rectangles that
are empty or have non-finite coordinates.

`pdf::ExtractRulingLines()` turns rectangles that are at most 4 px thick
and at least 8 px long into ruling lines along their centerline. Thicker
fills (cell shading, backgrounds) are ignored.

[FSA] Block write access to .mvn in sensitive path blocklist

Maven projects store build and JVM startup configuration in `.mvn`
directories (such as `.mvn/jvm.config`, `.mvn/maven.config`, and
`.mvn/extensions.xml`), and Maven's launcher walks upward from child
projects to discover ancestor `.mvn` directories.

This CL adds a suffix block rule for `*/.mvn` with
`BlockType::kBlockWrite` in `GenerateBlockPaths()`. This blocks save
and programmatic write operations targeting `.mvn` directories and
their descendants while continuing to allow read access, matching the
existing handling for `.git/hooks`, `.git/config`, and `.git/modules`.

[Gardener] Skip context menu BFCache test without BFCache

NoClickEventAfterNavigationToBackForwardCache in
ExtensionContextMenuActiveTabBrowserTest assumes a cross-site
navigation places `old_frame` into the back/forward cache. On
`linux-bfcache-rel`, `bf_cache_browser_tests` runs with
`--disable-features=BackForwardCache`, so `old_frame` is destroyed on
navigation and `old_frame->IsInLifecycleState(...)` dereferences null.

Skip the test when `BackForwardCache::IsBackForwardCacheFeatureEnabled`
is false.

[Code Health] Use base::FindOrNull in DeviceDataManagerX11

Replace redundant map lookups (such as find() != end() followed by
operator[], and .contains() followed by .at()) with base::FindOrNull
across DeviceDataManagerX11. Also hoist loop-invariant lookups on
valuator_count_ and data_type_lookup_ outside of event processing loops.

GetEventData() and GetDataRange() now also bounds-check |type| against
the per-device valuator vector, consistent with HasEventData(). This is
not a behavior change in practice, as those vectors are always sized to
DT_LAST_ENTRY.

[TabUI] Wire selection and pin state in GroupedTabListDataProvider

Tab selection, multi-selection, and pin state changes in TabModel must
update the grouped data provider so delegates and viewholders reflect
item state changes without requiring full list rebuilds.

In collapsed-only mode (GROUPED), selecting a tab inside a group
resolves to and selects the composite group card. Switching between tabs
within the same group drops redundant notifications to avoid thumbnail
refetches and card churn. In expandable mode (NESTED), selection targets
the child tab directly and the group header remains unselected.

Multi-selection updates items matching the selected set with granular
MULTI_SELECTION payloads, while pin state updates dispatch PIN_STATE
payloads on standalone tabs.

[3p freshness] wayland-protocols: Remove the unused gtk dependency

third_party/wayland-protocols/gtk checks out the whole GTK repository
(pinned to 4.3.0 from 2021) only for gdk/wayland/protocol/gtk-shell.xml,
which the :gtk_shell_protocol target generates code for. Nothing has
depended on that target since ozone/wayland dropped GTK shell support
in https://crrev.com/c/6456400 (2025-04); `gn refs` finds no user on
Linux or ChromeOS. third_party/mutter builds its own copy of the
protocol from its own checkout.

Remove the gtk submodule, its DEPS and .gitmodules entries, the root
OWNERS entry for it, the unused target and its README.chromium section,
instead of setting up an autoroller for it.

[TWA] Wait for service worker before delivering POST share target

Preinstalled TWAs (e.g. Gmail/Chat/Drive on Android desktop) can be
installed without their page ever loading, so the web app's service
worker is never registered. A Web Share Target POST delivered to such
an app is not intercepted by a service worker, goes to the network,
and the shared data is lost (typically a 405 from the server).

When a POST share target is delivered, check whether a service worker
is registered for the share target action URL. If there is none, load
the app's launch URL (its start URL by default) in the same tab so the
page can register its service worker, wait for a service worker whose
scope matches the action URL to activate, then send the POST, replacing
the bootstrap history entry. A newly installed service worker activates
immediately and intercepts the subsequent main-frame navigation without
needing clients.claim(). If no service worker activates within a
timeout, the POST is sent anyway, preserving the previous behavior.

The timeout only runs while a page of the app's origin is committed, so
it is paused while the user is on another origin, e.g. a sign-in page
that the start URL redirected to. A service worker that activates while
on another origin sends the POST once a page of the app's origin
commits. The total wait is limited, after which the POST is dropped if
the tab is not on the app's origin.

The bootstrap URL is only used if it is an HTTP(S) URL with the same
origin as the share target action. The behavior is guarded by the
ShareTargetWaitForServiceWorker feature (enabled by default, with a
"timeout" param defaulting to 5s, and a "max_wait" param defaulting to
10m).

[Extensions] Fix chrome://extensions crash in site permissions dialog

DeveloperPrivateGetMatchingExtensionsForSiteFunction previously
iterated over all enabled extensions without checking whether each
extension should be displayed in extension settings. Consequently,
extensions that should not be displayed (such as component extensions
with host permissions) were returned in matchingExtensionsInfo, but were
not present in the WebUI extensions list.

When opening the site permissions edit dialog, an assertion failure
assert(this.extensionsIdToInfo_.has(id)) was triggered, crashing the
page.

This crash was surfaced in crbug.com/577822734 after we ramped up the ExtensionsToolbarAndMenuRedesign study to Stable. This study enables enhanced site access controls, which activates new code paths inside the chrome://extensions management page (specifically the site permissions dialog).

Fixed: 577822734

ff550ff253ae53b5293af79f90d533630c2ff543 [ diff ] 
Remove unnecessary fakeroot from Linux RPM builds

Building Linux RPM targets with DEPOT_TOOLS_USE_VIRTUAL_BUILD_PATH=1
fails during rpmbuild's %install phase when `cp -a` runs under fakeroot:

  cp: failed to preserve ownership for '...': Invalid argument

An unprivileged user cannot chown files to root; fakeroot uses a
LD_PRELOAD library (libfakeroot) to record fake root ownership in an
in-memory daemon, then invokes the real `fchownat()` syscall and ignores
an `EPERM` error. `DEPOT_TOOLS_USE_VIRTUAL_BUILD_PATH=1` runs the build
in a nested unprivileged user namespace  where only the caller's UID is
mapped and UID/GID 0 are unmapped. As a result, when `cp -a` uses
`fchownat(..., 0, 0)` to preserve the fake 0:0 owner reported by faked,
the syscall fails with `EINVAL`–which propagates back to `cp` and causes
the rpm build to fail.

However, rpm already declaratively sets file ownership to root in the
%files section, so the `fakeroot` wrapper is unnecessary. Remove it and
manually verify the RPM generated before and after this change is
bitwise-identical.

Fixed: 578118304

Revert "[Read Anything] Fix flaky AudioMenuElement accent menu close test"

This reverts commit 49c7d3dc969c3f27b16a1a5ac2a26e91bf4df7b4.

Reason for revert: Re-enabled ReadAnythingMochaTest.AudioMenu accent
menu test is still failing focus restoration assertions on
win11-arm64-rel-tests (expected null to equal <button>).

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/win11-arm64-rel-tests/9492/overview


Original change's description:
> [Read Anything] Fix flaky AudioMenuElement accent menu close test
>
> CrDialogElement.close() calls close() on the underlying native <dialog>
> element, which schedules its native 'close' event on the next animation
> frame via HTMLDialogElement::ScheduleCloseEvent() rather than in a
> microtask or 0ms timer.
>
> On slower or heavily loaded bots (such as win11-arm64-rel-tests),
> microtasksFinished() can resolve before the next animation frame fires
> the dialog's 'close' event, causing the assertion that <accent-menu> is
> removed to fail flakily.
>
> Await eventToPromise('close', accentMenu) before microtasksFinished()
> (matching the voice selection dialog test below it) and re-enable both
> tests in AudioMenuElement.
>

build: Remove use_reclient and reclient toolchain wrapper support

All builders and tools have migrated to Siso's built-in RBE client
and no longer set use_reclient. Remove the use_reclient GN argument,
rewrapper compiler prefix plumbing across gcc/apple/win toolchains,
the Siso reclient.star wrapper mode, and the use_reclient check in
ide_query.

Note that reclient_cfg_dir / use_reclient_cfgs (used by Siso on Mac/Win
until crbug.com/443838348 is resolved) and reclient_cros_cc_wrapper (still passed by chromite's cros_chrome_sdk.py) are retained for now.

🌺 Allow 1px rounding tolerance in ToolControllerScrollPageBrowserTest

After https://crrev.com/c/8531334 enabled `//chrome/browser/ttc/core:browser_tests`
in `android_browsertests`, `ToolControllerScrollPageBrowserTest` has
been consistently failing by 1 CSS pixel across 3 builds on 2 Primary
Android builders:
- `ToolControllerScrollPageBrowserTest.DocumentDownAndUpViewport` on
  `chrome/ci/android-desktop-17-arm64-rel-hylia-tests` (2/2 builds,
  every attempt: `1457` vs `1456`), e.g.:
  https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-desktop-17-arm64-rel-hylia-tests/1598
- `ToolControllerScrollPageBrowserTest.DocumentRightAndLeftViewport` on
  `chromium/ci/android-12l-x64-dbg-tests` (1/1 build, every attempt:
  `1343` vs `1342`), e.g.:
  https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/android-12l-x64-dbg-tests/45129

On Android devices with fractional device scale factors, Blink rounds
`document.scrollingElement.scrollHeight` and `clientHeight` (and
`scrollWidth` / `clientWidth`) independently to CSS-pixel integers
before subtraction, whereas `window.scrollY` / `window.scrollX` returns
the physical-pixel-clamped fractional maximum scroll offset rounded once
by `EvalInt` (`Math.round(...)`), producing a deterministic 1px
difference.

Use `EXPECT_NEAR(..., 1)` for the viewport max-scroll assertions so both
tests stay enabled on Android without needing to chain-revert
https://crrev.com/c/8551056 and https://crrev.com/c/8531334.

686f099f18e3c84990b4605374b670f5e0f3e9d0 [ diff ] 
[base] Gate task-dispatch ThreadCheckers on EXPENSIVE_DCHECKS_ARE_ON

On dcheck_always_on = true builds, 95.6% of all ThreadChecker CPU time
(2.22% out of 2.33% of total browser_tests CPU) comes from internal
base/ task-dispatch classes that run multiple thread checks on every
task execution, pump wake-up, and hang-watch scope transition:
- SequenceManager / ThreadControllerWithMessagePumpImpl
  (AssociatedThreadId, WorkTracker, and WorkIdProvider): 0.87% CPU
- WatchHangsInScope / HangWatchState / HangWatchDeadline: 0.72% CPU
- ThreadGroupImpl::WorkerDelegate: 0.63% CPU

Introduce EXPENSIVE_THREAD_CHECKER(), which expands to THREAD_CHECKER()
when EXPENSIVE_DCHECKS_ARE_ON() is true and to ThreadCheckerDoNothing
when DCHECK_IS_ON() && !EXPENSIVE_DCHECKS_ARE_ON(), with inline no-op
ScopedValidateThreadChecker overloads so Clang's compile-time
-Wthread-safety annotations (GUARDED_BY_CONTEXT, VALID_CONTEXT_REQUIRED)
remain enforced. Also move ~ScopedValidateThreadChecker() inline into
thread_checker.h (with an empty {} body rather than = default so Clang's
CFG still emits the UNLOCK_FUNCTION() destructor node) so non-LTO builds
elide the scope object completely without an out-of-line destructor
call.

Apply EXPENSIVE_THREAD_CHECKER() to these 3 internal base/ task-dispatch
subsystems while preserving 100% of SequenceChecker, WeakPtr, and
general ThreadChecker coverage on CQ.

This is a reland of commit 98926c59c978d505d87daba664288914286961da

The original change made
ClientCertificateBrowserTest.ProfileServiceIsCreatedAfterStartup fail,
because enabling CertificateCollectionEnabled created the profile's
CertificateProvisioningService during profile initialization. That is
fixed by the parent CL, which creates the client cert store lazily.

> feature, which enables collection of enterprise client certificates in
> Chrome security signals reports. This makes perf and test bots exercise
> the configuration that the CertificateCollectionEnabled Finch study
> will roll out on Windows, Mac, and Linux.

[Code Health] Use single map lookups in AnchoredNudgeManagerImpl

Replace redundant `contains()` and `operator[]` lookups on
`shown_nudges_` in `AnchoredNudgeManagerImpl` with single lookups using
`GetNudgeIfShown()`, and remove the associated TODO.

`PauseOrResumeDismissTimer()` is now a no-op when no timer exists for
`id`, instead of default-constructing one via `operator[]`.
`HandleNudgeWidgetDestroying()` now erases the anchor view observers
directly, so it no longer leaves empty entries behind in those maps.

JNI Zero: Include public jni_zero.h header

Headers in //third_party/jni_zero such as jni_unique_ptr.h,
jni_raw_ptr.h, and common_apis.h carry the IWYU pragma:

  // IWYU pragma: private, include "third_party/jni_zero/jni_zero.h"

and are re-exported by the public umbrella header
third_party/jni_zero/jni_zero.h. Replace direct includes of those
private headers outside //third_party/jni_zero with

[UI] Migrate components/services to `ui::mojom::WindowOpenDisposition`

Spell the type as `ui::mojom::WindowOpenDisposition` instead of the
deprecated `WindowOpenDisposition` alias, and include
"ui/base/mojom/window_open_disposition.mojom.h" instead of
"ui/base/window_open_disposition.h".

Headers that only use the type in declarations include the mojom
forward header instead.

Update DEPS for the new header.

No behavior change.

The C++ changes were generated by running the following from src/,
then `git cl format`; the DEPS changes were made by hand:

  migrate_window_open_disposition.py --migrate-type components/services
  check_alias_includes.py --enumerators components/services

The scripts are attached to https://crbug.com/373551504.

input_method: Remove g_browser_process from EditorGeolocationProviderFromFinch

Inject VariationsService into EditorGeolocationProviderFromFinch from
EditorMediatorFactory::BuildServiceInstanceForBrowserContext instead of
reading g_browser_process->variations_service() directly.

EditorGeolocationProviderFromFinch observes OnVariationsServiceDestroyed
to reset its VariationsService pointer before KeyedServices are torn
down during BrowserProcessImpl::StartTearDown().

Also update EditorMediatorFactory::BuildInstanceFor to accept an owned
EditorGeolocationProvider from the caller so QuickInsertClientImplTest
can inject EditorGeolocationMockProvider, and restrict browser_process.h
and global_features.h in chrome/browser/ash/input_method/DEPS to
editor_mediator_factory.cc.

from KioskSystemSession instead of looking it up through

Ash: Remove requestFileSystem auto-grant notification

When chrome.fileSystem.requestFileSystem() grants access automatically
to an auto-launched kiosk app, ConsentProviderImpl posts a notification
saying so. That notification has been invisible since 2018:
SessionStateNotificationBlocker hides every notification, in the
notification center and as a popup, while the session runs in app mode
(crrev.com/c/838702). The notification is only posted from auto-launched
kiosk apps, which always run in app mode, so nobody can see it. This CL
removes it instead of migrating it from NotificationDisplayService to
MessageCenter.

Access is still granted automatically, without a dialog, exactly as
before. Only the notification goes: its file, its strings and the
ShowNotification() method of ConsentProviderImpl::DelegateInterface.
The kRequestFileSystem notification catalog value is deprecated, not
renumbered.

Update the tests accordingly.

[TabUI] Wire tab and group reordering in GroupedTabListDataProvider

Tab moves and group reorders in TabModel must update the grouped data
provider so layout delegates and viewholders reflect item order changes
without full list resets.

In collapsed-only mode (GROUPED), standalone tab moves reposition the
tab card, while moving an entire group repositions the composite group
card. In expandable mode (NESTED), moving a group moves the group header
along with all its child tabs as a contiguous block.

Reordering tabs within a group repositions the child tab in expandable
mode and emits a granular TAB_GROUP_ORDER payload on the group card in
both modes so composite thumbnails can refresh without card rebuilds.

[Extensions] Fix flaky activity log policy tests on Windows

CountingPolicyTest and FullStreamUIPolicyTest ran activity log DB tasks
on the default BEST_EFFORT single-thread task runner. On Windows this is
a background-priority thread (THREAD_MODE_BACKGROUND_BEGIN), which also
lowers I/O priority, so SQLite operations on loaded bots could exceed
the 10s action timeout. Run the activity log task runner on the main
thread instead, as ActivityLogTest and ActivityDatabaseTest already do.

parent
2cf91fce47a4fb56420871058efdffe7582e67e0 [ diff ] 
webnn: Bypass mojo for tensor I/O on the in-renderer LiteRT path

When the LiteRT backend runs in-process in the renderer,
writeTensor()/readTensor() still went through the mojom WebNNTensor
interface, paying for BigBuffer allocation, mojo serialization, and a
cross-sequence hop even though both endpoints share an address space.
dispatch() itself was already zero-copy for this path (LiteRT wraps
BufferContent via TensorBuffer::CreateFromHostMemory), so all four
tensor-data memcpys were spent solely on the I/O boundary.

This removes BigBuffer allocation, any shared-memory setup, and mojo
serialization per writeTensor/readTensor call on the in-renderer path.
Two memcpys remain (script thread -> heap buffer -> BufferContent);
eliminating those is left for a follow-up. No mojom or behavior change
on the GPU-process path, and no new runtime flag — activated
automatically whenever a tensor is created via the in-renderer
provider.

6cc94f1d7858066848bf1aad5820d425d9cd7a18 [ diff ] 
[remoting] Restrict PC process filesystem access with Landlock

All Linux peer connection (PC) processes run as the same user. A PC
process is briefly dumpable at startup, before it calls
prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0), and on hosts with Yama ptrace_scope=0 (the
default on e.g. Debian and Fedora), another PC process could open its
/proc/<pid>/mem in that window. Seccomp-BPF cannot restrict paths, so
this CL adds a Landlock policy to PC processes.

The policy is applied at the start of PeerConnectionProcessMain(), while
the process is still single-threaded. It only allows read-only access
to the process' own /proc/self entries, CPU and memory information,
/etc, system libraries, the installation directory, the directory
/etc/resolv.conf points to (unless too broad), and /dev/urandom, plus
read-write access to /dev/null. All other filesystem access is denied,
including creating or writing files and the /proc entries of other
processes. Landlock also denies ptrace access checks to processes
outside of the Landlock domain. On Landlock ABI 6 and newer, signals
and abstract UNIX socket connections to processes outside of the
Landlock domain are denied as well.

If Landlock is not supported by the kernel, the PC process continues
without it, and logs a warning if Yama ptrace_scope is 0.

Mojo Java: Move decoding of struct & string arrays into the runtime

Shrinks Chrome's dex by ~3kb.

Decoding arrays of structs or strings previously generated a loop that
read the array header and each element pointer. This adds

each struct.

[remoting] Restrict cross-process syscalls in the Linux PC sandbox

All Linux peer connection (PC) processes run as the same user, so the
kernel's same-user permission checks do not separate them. This CL
extends the PC Seccomp-BPF blocklist so that a compromised PC process
cannot signal, inspect, or otherwise affect a sibling PC process:

* kill/tgkill may only target the calling process, otherwise the
  caller crashes. tkill is disallowed. rt_*sigqueueinfo to other
  processes fails with EPERM.
* prlimit64, get/setpriority, ioprio_* and sched_* may only target the
  calling process. For get/setpriority, ioprio_* and sched_*, the
  calling thread's ID is rewritten to 0 via a SIGSYS handler.
  PRIO_PGRP/PRIO_USER are denied.
* F_SETOWN/F_SETOWN_EX/FIOSETOWN/SIOCSPGRP, which can direct SIGIO to
  another process, are denied, as are F_SETSIG, TIOCSTI and TIOCSPGRP.
* pidfd_open returns ENOSYS. pidfd_getfd, pidfd_send_signal,
  process_madvise, process_mrelease, get_robust_list, move_pages and
  migrate_pages are denied.
* prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, non-zero) and PR_SET_PDEATHSIG are denied, so
  the process cannot become dumpable again or outlive the daemon.
* Keyrings, System V IPC and POSIX message queues, which are shared
  by all processes of the same user, are denied.
* io_uring returns ENOSYS. bpf, userfaultfd, perf_event_open and
  fanotify_init are denied. fchmodat2 is denied like fchmodat.
* Syscalls newer than the newest one known to the policy return
  ENOSYS, so new syscalls are not silently allowed.

The Crashpad client now leaves SIGSYS to the sandbox, which installs
its own SIGSYS handler to emulate or deny syscalls.

The stale comment about /dev/shm is also updated: base allocates shared
memory with memfd_create.

[ContextualTasks] Deflake composebox Mocha tests

Composebox Mocha tests previously mounted a full app element that
triggered an initial guest webview navigation on every test case, and
packed up to eight test cases into a single browser test invocation,
causing debug builds to exceed the per-test timeout. Stubbing out the
initial pending URL load in the composebox test helper eliminates the
guest process overhead, and splitting the auto-tab deletion and voice
coherence suites halves the work per browser test so auto-tab deletion
semantics can be re-enabled on Linux.

WebXR: Always force layer shared images to clear

When WebXR layers are created the developer can request that they
not be cleared every frame with the `clearOnAccess` init arg. This
doesn't work for layers backed by a shared image, though, since we
don't know currently if the shared images are recycled and have
been cleared at least once previously. As such, force layers that
use a shared image to always clear until we can track their cleared
state better.

[remoting] Re-enable EvaluateCapabilityTest.ShouldReturnCrashResult

EvaluateCapabilityTest.ShouldReturnCrashResult was disabled in 2017
(crrev.com/c/592009) after failing on non-DCHECK CI builders
(crbug.com/749913). At that time, EvaluateCrash() called NOTREACHED()
followed by `return 0;`, and NOTREACHED() was a no-op when DCHECKs were
disabled, causing the subprocess to exit with 0 instead of crashing.

NOTREACHED() is now [[noreturn]] and unconditionally terminates the
process in all build configurations, so EvaluateCrash() in
capability_test_stub_main.cc reliably exits with a non-zero status.
Remove the DISABLED_ prefix to re-enable the test.

Could not reproduce the original failure locally because NOTREACHED()
now crashes unconditionally across all build configurations. Verified
with 100 parallel local iterations (--test-launcher-bot-mode
--gtest_repeat=100) and the full EvaluateCapabilityTest suite with 0
failures.

[WebAudio] Shrink ReverbConvolverStage::pre_delay_buffer_

`ReverbConvolverStage` always allocates `fft_size` frames for
`pre_delay_buffer_`, even though `Process()` only needs
`pre_delay_length_` frames (at most `fft_size / 2`).

This CL sizes `pre_delay_buffer_` to `pre_delay_length_`, and always
uses `temporary_buffer_` as the scratch buffer in `Process()`.

For example, when a `ConvolverNode` uses a 3s mono or stereo impulse
response at 48kHz, `Reverb` creates 2 convolvers of 42 stages each (up
to FFT size 8192). This shrinks their `pre_delay_buffer_` allocations
from 2.25 MiB to ~514 KiB, saving ~1.75 MiB (~78%).

Mojo Java: Track struct depth per Decoder & pass Decoders to handlers

Shrinks Chrome's dex by ~2kb.

 * Every generated struct decode() ended with decreaseStackDepth().
   Instead, each Decoder now tracks its struct depth, which is copied
   to child Decoders (each struct is decoded with its own Decoder).
   The limit is still 100 nested structs, as before.
 * Stub and ForwardToCallback now pass a Decoder to generated code
   rather than a Message, so that "new Decoder(message)" is not
   inlined for every method.

Behavior is unchanged.

[DataSharing] Keep migration KeyValueData alive until DB shutdown

MigrationStateDatabaseImpl::Init() passes an unretained pointer to
migration_state_data_ into InitOnDBSequence() on db_task_runner_,
relying on ~MigrationStateDatabaseImpl() to keep database objects
alive until all queued DB tasks finish. However, unlike
MessagingBackendDatabaseImpl::~MessagingBackendDatabaseImpl(),
~MigrationStateDatabaseImpl() posted the shutdown task with PostTask()
instead of PostTaskAndReply() and let migration_state_data_ be
destroyed immediately on the main sequence. If the database was
destroyed before InitOnDBSequence() ran, InitOnDBSequence()
dereferenced the already freed KeyValueData on db_task_runner_.

To preserve the cross-sequence lifetime contract, use
PostTaskAndReply() in ~MigrationStateDatabaseImpl() and move
migration_state_data_ into the reply closure so that it is destroyed
on the main sequence only after all tasks on db_task_runner_ have
completed.

[remoting] Harden PC process startup on Linux

The Linux peer connection (PC) processes all run as the same user and
handle untrusted network traffic. This CL hardens their startup:

* Make the PC process non-dumpable as soon as its process type is
  known, so that other processes running as the same user cannot
  inspect or modify it via ptrace or procfs. The Crashpad handler
  retains CAP_SYS_PTRACE, so crash dumps keep working.
* Never spawn a Crashpad handler from the PC process. Without the
  handler socket passed by the daemon, crash reporting is disabled.
  A self-spawned handler would run unsandboxed as the shared user and
  outlive the PC process.
* Fail to start the PC process if the multi-threaded Seccomp-BPF
  sandbox is not supported, instead of running unsandboxed.

Add allowlisted interpreter script extractor for process attribution

When attributing enterprise security events to external processes, the
process executable is often a language runtime or shell interpreter
(e.g. node, python3, bash) where the relevant actor path is the script
file argument in argv.

Implement allowlisted interpreter script extraction in
components/enterprise/connectors/core/:
- Add IsAllowlistedInterpreter():
  - Normalize executable basenames using base::FilePath and
    base::TrimString() to strip optional .exe extensions and trailing
    version/punctuation characters (e.g. python3.12, node20, ruby3.2,
    perl5.34), and match against allowlisted interpreter families
    (node, nodejs, python, bash, sh, zsh, ruby, perl, deno, bun).
    Non-interpreter binaries omit script_path.
- Add ExtractInterpreterScript():
  - Omit script_path when known inline execution or stdin/module flags
    are present before the script target or '--' (-c, -lc, -ec, -s for
    shells; -e, -E, --eval, -p, --print, -m, --module, -i,
    --interactive, eval, repl, or bare '-' stdin for runtimes).
  - Fail closed in LooksLikeScriptTarget() by requiring a valid
    base::FilePath without parent references, tilde prefixes, URL
    schemes, or shell/query characters whose final extension matches
    allowlisted script extensions (.js, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .mts, .cts,
    .jsx, .tsx, .py, .pyw, .pyc, .sh, .bash, .zsh, .rb, .pl, .pm).
  - Return the sanitized script path via SanitizeProcessPath(), failing
    closed if base::DIR_HOME cannot be resolved.
- Add unit tests in process_extractor_unittest.cc.

Printing: Ignore failed records in Emf::Record::SafePlayback()

https://crrev.com/1644212 updated Emf::SafePlaybackProc() to return 0
when Emf::Record::SafePlayback() returns false, which causes
EnumEnhMetaFile() to abort enumeration of the entire EMF page if any
single record fails validation or GDI playback. This is too strict for
real world use, as seen in the associated bug report.

To relax the code while still guarding against malformed record, update
Emf::Record::SafePlayback() and Emf::Record::Play() to return void and
ignore failed or malformed individual records (similar to
PostScriptMetaFile::SafePlayback()), so Emf::SafePlaybackProc()
continues enumerating the remaining records on the page as long as the
record's outer size boundaries are valid.

Add EmfTest.SafePlayback and EmfTest.SafePlaybackSkipsInvalidRecords to
verify that Emf::SafePlayback() plays valid records and skips invalid
ones without aborting the rest of the metafile.

chromecast: Clean up preference process-separation and migration logic

The `ProcessType` / `FILE_CAST_BROWSER_CONFIG` split, `migration_utils`,
and `CastFeatureUpdateObserver` (`feature_update.mojom`) were added for
an older `external_mojo`-based `cast_browser` decoupling design. In the
current architecture, `cast_service` does not use this Chromium
`PrefService` code, and the Cast web runtime always loads preferences
and DCS feature flags directly from `FILE_CAST_CONFIG`
(`--use-cast-browser-pref-config` is unused).

Specifically, this CL:
- Simplifies `PrefServiceHelper` and `CastFeatureListCreator` to always
  load `FILE_CAST_CONFIG`, removing `ProcessType`,
  `FILE_CAST_BROWSER_CONFIG`, and `chromecast/browser/migration/`.
- Removes `CastFeatureUpdateObserver`, `feature_update.mojom`, and the
  unused decoupling/broker command-line switches (`kDeferFeatureList`,
  `kUseCastBrowserPrefConfig`, `kInProcessBroker`,
  `kCastMojoBrokerPath`).
- Removes `external_mojo` broker/connector initialization and obsolete
  `ServiceManagerContext` / `CastContentBrowserClient` service-hosting
  hooks from `chromecast/browser`.
- Removes unused `//chromecast/external_mojo/external_service_support`
  dependencies and the unused `CmaBackendFactory::Create()` declaration
  from `chromecast/media`.

Omit unknown source code location in inspector CSP issue

When GatherSecurityPolicyViolationEventData() collects the CSP
violation event data into SecurityPolicyViolationEventInit, it
treats the received source location as unknown if its line number
is zero, so ContentSecurityPolicy::ReportViolation dispatches and
reports the violation without a source location.

But GatherSecurityPolicyViolationEventData() returned the source
location as is, so the inspector CSP issue got a source code location
with a non-empty URL and an unknown line number (-1 in the protocol)
for the violation (e.g. a CSS background image fetched by style
recalculation after the document is parsed).

Return null when GatherSecurityPolicyViolationEventData() receives an
unknown source location, so that the inspector CSP issue omits the
sourceCodeLocation field for the violation.

ddb331eea9484e40a8a0a1f0f446150b4345fd57 [ diff ] 
Skip CSP check on inline handler set in document without window

Fix a regression the commit f5f363bd6bba6d155cfbc24f14f862cd60644baf
introduced - false-positive CSP violation on the active document for an
inline event handler attribute set in a document without a browsing
context (e.g. a document created by DOMParser.parseFromString, an owner
document of template contents).

ShouldBlockInlineScriptAttributeSet() checked allow-inline by using
the CSP in the element's ExecutionContext, which is the active
document's window that holds the CSP list for the active document. But
a document without a browsing context has an empty CSP list.

So ShouldBlockInlineScriptAttributeSet() now gets the CSP from the
element's document's window, and does not block nor report when there
is no window.

remoting: Add warm-up encode before timing in encoder benchmark

InitializeEncoderOnEncodeThread() previously only constructed the
WebrtcVideoEncoder wrapper, leaving thread-local allocator caches, SIMD
dispatch tables, and code pages cold until the first timed keyframe
encode.

Perform a single warm-up encode on a temporary encoder instance during
InitializeEncoderOnEncodeThread() before creating the benchmark encoder
and starting the timer, warming the encode thread without altering the
rate-control state of the benchmark run.

Tag: crd-encoder-benchmark

[Find in Page] Add asymmetric diacritic search

Previously, case-insensitive Find-in-Page ignored all diacritics, so
searching for accented characters (e.g., 'ä', 'é', 'ö', 'č') matched
every unaccented base character on the page. This change adds support
(guarded behind `FindInPageAsymmetricDiacriticSearch`, disabled by
default) for Unicode TR10 asymmetric search so unmarked base
characters still match accented variants, while accented characters
only match that specific diacritic.

Screenshots: https://crbug.com/40518349#comment70

Bug: 40518349
Test: blink_unittests --gtest_filter="TextSearcherIcuTest.*:FindInPageTest.*"

Exclude date/time autofill preview text from copy and drag

While an Autofill suggestion is previewed, date, month, week, time and
datetime-local inputs render the would-be value as text in their UA
shadow tree. That text was selectable so copy, cut and selection drags
serialized it into text/plain, letting a page read previewed data, such
as a stored card's expiration date, from dragstart before the user
accepted the suggestion. Make the previewed date/time pseudo-elements
unselectable and read-only in the UA stylesheet, matching the <select>
and text control previews. Accepted autofilled values are still copied.

e23534c649274ef2b6d854da9c299a21b3177c5d [ diff ] 
Reland "[WebXR] Don't draw the immersive overlay before its graphics are ready"

This is a reland of commit 07350d3d4eeb10bc22254989d9fd58b9199b09d7

The new test, WebXrVrOpenXrBrowserTest.TestPromptWhileIndicatorsVisible,
crashed in android_browsertests. Its last step waited for
kWebXrExternalPromptNotification to become visible, but
UiSceneCreator::CreateExternalPromptNotificationOverlay() creates that
element only on desktop, so Ui::GetElementVisibility() dereferenced a
null element. The crash came after the overlay restart and the frames
that followed it.

The test now checks the prompt notification only on desktop. On every
platform it first waits for the restarted overlay's BrowserRenderer
(UiUtils::Create()) and a few frames, then ends the session, so it still
covers the restart race on Android. The renderer thread change is
unchanged. This also fixes the spelling of
UiSceneCreator::CreateExternalPromptNotificationOverlay().

Original change's description:
> [WebXR] Don't draw the immersive overlay before its graphics are ready
>
> VRBrowserRendererThread restarts the overlay (StopOverlay() then
> StartOverlay()) when its draw state changes or its graphics context is
> lost, and StartOverlay() creates the GraphicsDelegate asynchronously.
> Until it's ready, `graphics_` is null but `started_` is true, and an
> overlay pose or frame submission from before the restart can still
> arrive:
>
> * SubmitResult() requested the next overlay pose because `started_` was
>   set.
> * OnPose(), for a pose requested before the restart, called
>   graphics_->SetXrViews() on null; only a DCHECK guarded it.
>
> VRUiHostImpl::ShowExternalNotificationPrompt() restarts the overlay this
> way in one task when a permission prompt appears while the capture
> indicators are showing: it hides the indicators, which stops the overlay,
> and then shows the prompt notification, which starts it again. The
> overlay draws every frame while the indicators show, so a pose request or
> a submission is almost always in flight.
>
> SubmitResult() now requests a pose only once the graphics exist, and
> OnPose() ignores a pose that arrives before them. OnGraphicsReady()
> already runs the pending overlay update, which requests a new pose.
>

In Pinning v2, the unpinned contextual tasks toolbar button becomes
visible in its active state as soon as the side panel opens, and
transitions to its collapsed (ephemeral thread) state when the side
panel closes.

ContextualTasks.EphemeralToolbarButton.Shown and only starts the
ShownDuration timer when entering the collapsed state.

remoting: Scale default benchmark bitrate by resolution

webrtc_video_encoder_benchmark previously used a flat 5000 kbps
default bitrate across all resolutions (1080p, 1440p, 4K). At 1440p
and 4K, EncoderBitrateFilter floored VP8/VP9 to 2500 kbps/MP (9216
kbps at 1440p, 20736 kbps at 4K) while AV1 (1000 kbps/MP floor)
remained at 5000 kbps at 1440p and 8294 kbps at 4K.

When bitrate_kbps is not explicitly set in the JSON configuration,
scale the default target bitrate at 2500 kbps per megapixel (with a
1000 kbps minimum) based on the active frame dimensions.

[glic] Keep loading state when finishLoading timer fires while hidden

When chrome://glic loads while the panel is hidden, GlicAppController's
finishLoading() timer (after kPreHoldLoadingTimeMs +
kMinHoldLoadingTimeMs) unconditionally transitioned WebUiState to
kWarmed even when the web client had not warmed or initialized yet.
Entering kWarmed hides the loading panel and shows the uninitialized
guest panel without a header, and switches the subsequent open timeout
from kClientLoadTimeout to kWarmedTimeout.

Match guestLoaded() by leaving the controller in kFinishLoading when the
panel is hidden, and start the client load timeout in updatePageState()
once the panel becomes visible if the web client still has not warmed or
become ready.

Update GlicLegacyWebviewWarmedNativeLoadingBrowserTest, which asserted
the old hidden kWarmed transition, to expect kFinishLoading while hidden
and the native placeholder on reopen, and refresh the matching comment
in Host::ComputeIsShowingNativeLoading().

gamepad: Gate user activation on page focus

NavigatorGamepad::Gamepads() minted kInteraction user activation on page
visibility alone (IsPageVisible()) without checking whether the page has
focus. Because gamepad input is fanned out to all polling renderers
across the system regardless of which window or application has focus,
gamepad button presses directed at another window forged user activation
in unfocused visible pages.

Gate user activation in NavigatorGamepad::Gamepads() on page focus via
GetFocusController().IsFocused(), guarded by the
GamepadUserActivationFocus runtime-enabled feature as a killswitch.
Checking page-level focus blocks unfocused windows from gaining user
activation while still allowing iframe-embedded games in a focused tab
to receive activation without a prior click inside the iframe.

[downloads] Remove completed downloads older than 90 days from history

DownloadHistory::LoadHistoryDownloads is a top source of jank. It
creates one DownloadItem per row of the downloads table, and completed
downloads are never removed from that table unless the user (or an
extension) erases them. On Windows Canary/Dev, 8% of profile loads
instantiate over 1,000 DownloadItems (P99 = 12k), but only 3% would if
downloads started more than 90 days ago were excluded [1].

This CL adds the kRemoveOldDownloadsFromHistory feature, disabled by
default. When enabled, LoadHistoryDownloads removes completed downloads
started more than RemoveOldDownloadsFromHistoryMinAge (default: 90
days) ago from the history DB, instead of creating DownloadItems for
them. Downloaded files are not deleted.

Cancelled and interrupted downloads are left untouched, because
DownloadManagerImpl::ShouldClearDownloadFromDB already clears them after
90 days, and also deletes their partial files.

[1] Download.History.DownloadCount.PostRemoval{,.Last90Days}, Windows
    Canary+Dev, builds >= 158.0.8109, last 7 days.

WebContents: Key the Java peer by ID instead of native address

WebContentsImpl was found from C++ and from a Parcel by the address of
its WebContentsAndroid. A Parcel written before the peer was destroyed,
for example by clearNativeReference(), resolved to whichever
WebContentsAndroid was later allocated at the same address.

Give each WebContentsImpl a peer ID that is never reused within the
process, and use it as the key of the Java-side peer map, the value
written into the Parcel, and the argument WebContentsAndroid passes to
getJavaObject(). Deserialization is now a Java-only lookup, so
fromNativePtr() and the set of allocated WebContentsAndroids are
removed.

`CanTriggerPinningPromoForAiPage` requires the current task to have an
associated webpage resource and the AI page URL to include an `mstk`
query parameter, which landed just before the onboarding tooltip

onboarding tooltip is hidden.

parent
fb9fe7be8448aaefe3b6d15eb2d2d0798f44e297 [ diff ] 
[TabStrip] Handle tab groups when dropping links on the tab strip (3/6)

Make link drops onto the tab strip aware of tab groups.
-A new tab joins a group when it's inserted right before one of the
 group's tabs, i.e. between two tabs of that group or right after the
 group's expanded title. Dropping at the trailing edge of a group
 doesn't grow it.
-Over a collapsed group title, the leading half inserts before the
 group and the trailing half inserts after it, since the group's tabs
 are hidden. This matches desktop.
-The tab is merged with TabModel#mergeListOfTabsToExistingGroup using
 an index computed before the tab is created, so it lands exactly at
 the drop position.

Ignore the parts of unpinned views hidden under the pinned tabs.
-Unpinned views scroll under the pinned tabs, so a drop at the end of
 the pinned tabs could insert before a hidden tab rather than the
 partially visible one.
-Now, only the visible part of an unpinned view is used to decide
 whether the drop is before or after it.

Prevent ProgressClamping from growing CSSMathExpressionOperation

Since 59da575a760b1, CSSMathExpressionOperation has a ProgressClamping
field. This enum has an int-sized underlying type (4 bytes) which does
not fit in the two bytes of tail padding that the object had. As a
result, the size of the object grows from 48 to 56 bytes in release
builds. Oilpan adds an 8-byte header to every object, so the required
allocation grows from 56 to 64 bytes, moving it into the next size
class.

This size increase has the side effect of making
blink_perf.events/EventsDispatching run about 10% slower on
mac-m2-pro-perf, even though the CL does not directly change any code
that runs during event dispatch. Pinpoint tests show that this
regression disappears when the size of the object is kept at its
previous 48 bytes.

Use uint8_t as the underlying type of ProgressClamping, so that the
field fits in the existing padding and the object is back to 48 bytes.
The benchmark recovers from 2091 to about 2349 runs/s.
